fixes.explanation: Close, but that's not how Paul puts it. He calls the first glory "…what was fading away…" For the greater glory he says it's "…that which endures!" Fading and enduring are the two sides he sets against each other.

That's what Paul says. Moses would put a veil over his face "…to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away." The glory on his face was fading, and the veil kept them from gazing at the end of it. I think that's a lot like covering a cookie tray with a towel so nobody watches the last of the steam rise. Paul gives the reason himself, so we can take it straight from him.

Paul says the veil "…has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed." It's not removed by trying harder, and it's not removed by reading it again. He says it's only in Christ. My mustache can't lift that veil, friend, and neither can anyone else's.

That's actually where Paul says the veil stays. He says, "…even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts." Reading Moses again is where the veil remains, and turning to the Lord is where it's taken away. Hearing Moses read doesn't lift it, friend. Turning to the Lord does.

That's not what Paul says in this verse. He says that all of us who reflect the glory of the Lord with unveiled faces "…are being transformed into His image…" Being sent out to all nations isn't mentioned here. I'll admit it sounds like a fine batch of news, friend, but this verse is about being transformed.

Paul says the fading belongs to the glory on Moses' face (2 Corinthians 3:7). About the glory we reflect, he says we "…are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit." He doesn't say that glory fades. So the statement puts the fading in the wrong place.
